title: treesitter C Syntax Highlight Crash with SIGSEGV in ts_query_cursor_next_capture

labels.name: bug-crash
labels.description: issue reporting a crash or segfault

body:
I came across this reproducible crash while pasting some non-code text into a .c file. I've put a minimal version of the text that causes the crash in this issue. I was able to reproduce this with both the nightly build (v0.5.0-dev+1256-gd19348923) and the Debug build that I built.

I hope I created this in the correct project as it involves neovim, nvim-treesitter, treesitter and tree-sitter-c.

- `nvim --version`:
```
# ~/neovim/bin/nvim --version
NVIM v0.5.0-dev+1256-gd19348923
Build type: Debug
LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3
Compilation: /usr/bin/cc -g -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wno-unused-parameter -Wstrict-prototypes -std=gnu99 -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wmissing-prototypes -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wvla -fstack-protector-strong -fno-common -fdiagnostics-color=auto -DINCLUDE_GENERATED_DECLARATIONS -D_GNU_SOURCE -DNVIM_MSGPACK_HAS_FLOAT32 -DNVIM_UNIBI_HAS_VAR_FROM -DMIN_LOG_LEVEL=1 -I/home/vzaa/Downloads/neovim/build/config -I/home/vzaa/Downloads/neovim/src -I/home/vzaa/Downloads/neovim/.deps/usr/include -I/usr/include -I/home/vzaa/Downloads/neovim/build/src/nvim/auto -I/home/vzaa/Downloads/neovim/build/include
Compiled by vzaa@t490o

Features: +acl +iconv +tui
See ":help feature-compile"
``` 
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: ) behaves differently?
Yes, requires treesitter with syntax enabled
- Operating system/version:
Ubuntu 20.04.2
- Terminal name/version:
MATE Terminal 1.24.0
- `$TERM`:
xterm-256color


### Steps to reproduce
1. Install `nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter` similar to  #13129, in my case with vim-plug with the minimal config file:
```
call plug#begin('~/.vim/plugged')
Plug 'nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter', {'do': ':TSUpdate'}
call plug#end()

lua <<EOF
require'nvim-treesitter.configs'.setup { ensure_installed = "c", highlight = { enable = true}, }
EOF
```
2. Put the following text in example.c
```c
1: A.X_Obj.B.C.2.Enable: true
1: A.X_Obj.B.C.2.Enable: true
1: A.X_Obj.B.C.2.Enable: true
1: A.X_Obj.B.C.2.Enable: true

1: A.X_Obj.B.C.2.Enable: true
1: A.X_Obj.B.C.2.Enable: true
1: A.X_Obj.B.C.2.Enable: true
```
3. Open with nvim:
```
$ ~/neovim/bin/nvim example.c
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

### Expected behaviour
Even though the text is not valid C code it should not crash neovim
